acceptance: Scheduled start times for both workflows over at least 7 days are recorded with the delay from cron and the fork-to-core gap for each day.

Either core delivery runs whenever the fork publishes a new wheel (an event or dispatch from the fork's delivery step), so ordering no longer depends on schedule timing, or the measurement shows the order held every day and the docs state the expected worst-case adoption latency.
The operator docs (fork downstream/MAINTAINING.md and core's SQLGlot delivery doc) state the real latency from upstream tag to core adoption instead of the cron times alone.
context:
Decision gate: adding a fork-to-core trigger crosses repositories and changes who can start the core delivery run. Present the options to the owner before implementing: (a) document the latency only; (b) the fork's delivery job dispatches core sqlglot-delivery.yml after a wheel is published, using an App token limited to actions:write on core; (c) core polls more often (for example every 6 hours). No change is made without the owner's choice.

Verification rubric: (1) the 7-day measurement comes from the Actions API (created_at of event=schedule runs), not estimates; (2) for option (b), a test or dry run shows the dispatch happens only after a successful publish, and a real fork publish starts a core run within minutes; (3) core's existing delivery tests and the workflow trust-root tests pass; (4) docs name the measured latency.

Guardrails: do not remove the daily schedules, which stay as the fallback; do not widen the fork App's core permissions beyond starting this one workflow; do not weaken the delivery workflow's trust-root checks or its workflow_run branch filter (#4233); do not change Theseus. Heavy or long test runs go through make heavy-run.

Owner decision 2026-11-17 (choice dialog): option (c). Run core sqlglot-delivery.yml every 6 hours (cron '37 0,6,12,18 * * *') and document the measured delay from upstream tag to adoption in the fork and core docs. No fork-to-core dispatch and no new App permissions.

2026-11-17: delivered under the owner's option (c). Core: https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4287, squash-merged as 5da8697593341e37a6ba4cfc50502df3f87a7070. sqlglot-delivery.yml cron '37 6 * * *' -> '37 0,6,12,18 * * *'; nothing else in the workflow changed (the workflow_run chore/sqlglot-** filter is kept). docs/internal/release-guide.md states the 6-hour cadence, the measured 7-10 h schedule delay, that nothing orders core after the fork, and the worst-case adoption delay (about 6 h plus schedule delay). New test test_the_schedule_runs_at_least_every_six_hours expands each cron entry to minutes of the day and requires every gap, including the wrap past midnight, to be at most 6 h; 44 workflow tests pass; a review finding about whole-hour comparison was fixed (c95b8c55c). Fork: https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot/pull/95, merged as ce17aa00d98184dd11a4492a0df80899678cc1fc, adds a Timing paragraph to downstream/MAINTAINING.md with the same numbers. Rubric: (1) measurement from the Actions API created_at of schedule runs: fork started 12:30Z-13:59Z (2026-11-10..16), core 13:46Z-16:48Z (2026-11-09..16), fork-to-core gap 1.3-3.3 h; (2) option (b) not chosen, no fork-to-core trigger; (3) core workflow tests pass; (4) both docs name the measured delay.
description: The fork controller benchbox-upstream.yml (cron '41 5 * * *') started its scheduled runs between 12:30Z and 13:59Z on 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-16. Core sqlglot-delivery.yml (cron '37 6 * * *') started between 13:46Z and 16:48Z on 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-16. The design assumes the fork runs about an hour before core, so a release merged by the fork is adopted the same day. In the observed week core always started after the fork, but only because the delays happened to line up; the gaps were 1.3 to 3.3 hours and nothing enforces the order. If core runs first, adoption waits a full day. The cause (GitHub delaying scheduled runs under load, as recorded in oracle-sweep-schedules-dropped-by-github-20261101) is an inference.
